newsitem.title: POLAND: Commerzbank unlikely to take over BRE.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank unlikely to take over BRE.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG does not want to up its stake in Bank Rozwoju Eksportu (BRE) to over 50 percent, despite Polish Securities Commission's (KPW) approval, BRE's president said on Monday.

Commerzbank, which currently has 32.8 percent of BRE, planned to increase its stake to 48.8 percent by acquiring a new 4.5-million-share issue, but it was cleared by KPW to gain more than 50 percent if it resulted from a public tender offer.
"Commerzbank doesn't intend to take a majority stake in BRE," Krzysztof Szwarc said.
He added the tender was likely to be called in April 1998.
"We are working on the prospectus and I think 10 days before the end of June we will send it (to the KPW), and my intuition tells me we will call the tender in April next year," he said.
Under Polish securities trading law any shareholder acquiring more than 33 percent control of the company is obliged by law to offer to buy all remaining shares from other shareholders.
Szwarc also said the bank's net profit could rise to 130 million zlotys from last year's 114.7 million zlotys.
"In the (first) five months (of 1997) we had 52 million zlotys, if the pace was maintained it would be 130 million zlotys (in the whole 1997)," he said.
